text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: p99 latency spike observed in eu-dedicated pool (dedicated-eu-3). Paging oncall.
alex_cheng: acked. looking now — any customer-visible errors?
maria_garcia: p95 ~ 280ms, p99 jumped to 7.2s for generation endpoints. streaming stalls reported for chat/streaming routes. rough start ~ 1755556720 UTC.
benji: seeing queue depth climb on the dedicated-eu-3 router from 20 -> 900 in ~3m. backlog is mostly hotshot (low priority) + some customer traffic.
sam_ops: autoscaler fired at 1755556745 but new provisioned slots stayed in PROVISIONING for >90s; handshake to runtime failing with handshake_ttl_exceeded logs.
tara_ml: looks like KV-cache coldpath is hitting hard on those newly provisioned slots — lots of cache misses, tokenization path slow. streaming stalls align with cold KV fills.
alex_cheng: any recent deploys to that pool?
deploy-bot: deploy 2026.03.15-rls-321 rolled to eu-dedicated nodes at 1755556660 — no rollback.
maria_garcia: correlating: deploy started ~9m before spike, but spike onset is after autoscaler attempts. hypothesis: scale handshake + cold cache = compounding tail latency.
benji: also see slot-provision jitter logs: "slot_assigned -> booted -> handshake_timeout -> slot_deleted" repeated. suspiciously high image pull times from registry eu1.
sam_ops: can we reroute some traffic to dedicated-eu-2? fallback policy exists but not enabled automatically because routing policy prefers local region.
tara_ml: rapid mitigation: enable fallback routing to eu-dedicated-warm (higher latency but warmed) for generation routes.
alex_cheng: doing that now: `redwoodctl route set-fallback --from dedicated-eu-3 --to dedicated-eu-warm --routes generation,chat` — applied.
cs_lead: FYI CS — initial customer impact: 4 enterprise tenants saw >20% request retries, several support tickets created. ETA for curtailing impact?
benji: after switching fallback, p99 dropped from 7.2s -> 1.1s for affected routes. queue depth starting to drain :thumbsup:
maria_garcia: mitigation helped but we still have root cause to address: why provisioning queued slots didn't finish. early logs show registry timeouts and intermittent NTP drift on nodes causing handshake TTL mismatches.
sam_ops: I'm kicking a soft-restart on the autoscaler controller to clear any stuck allocations: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/autoscaler-controller`.
alex_cheng: restarting now — will monitor.
benji: also bumped per-slot prewarm threshold for that pool (experimental): `pool-config set --pool eu-dedicated-3 --prewarm 2` — this should keep a minimal warmed margin while we investigate.
tara_ml: note: prewarm helps streaming stalls but increases cost; we should only keep it while root cause is fixed.
deploy-bot: autoscaler-controller restart succeeded at 1755556788.
alex_cheng: autoscaler now showing healthy allocations; new slots moved to READY and handshake completed cleanly around 1755556810.
maria_garcia: p99 now ~ 220ms, streaming stalls resolved. queue depth back to baseline.
cs_lead: customer update: send a short note: impacted customers experienced transient retries 1755556720-1755556820 UTC, mitigated, no data loss. I'll draft.
cs_lead: draft: "We experienced an increase in latency on EU dedicated capacity for ~2 minutes; we routed traffic to warmed standby capacity and the issue was resolved. We're investigating root cause and will follow up." ok?
alex_cheng: LGTM. tag legal? maybe not yet.
benji: next steps: 1) postmortem owner: sam_ops + maria_garcia. 2) root-cause analysis on registry timeouts + slot handshake TTL mismatch. 3) short-term: keep prewarm=2 for eu-dedicated-3 for 1 hour then revert via automation.
tara_ml: add eval to detect KV coldpath amplification during scale events — add metric: kv_miss_ratio_during_scale.
sam_ops: paging handoff in 10m — I'll leave summary and follow-up actions in ops-runbook and escalate to infra if registry shows persistent latency.
alex_cheng: thanks everyone. going to mark incident as mitigated. oncall handoff to next shift: @maria_garcia, @sam_ops to follow for RCA.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: Mitigation applied and p99 returned to SLO. Follow-up: create postmortem and runbook updates.
cs_lead: noted, will file a proactive outreach for customers hit. :eyes:
